text:
If you’re paying privately, I’d prioritize therapists who **specialize in OCD and regularly use ERP (Exposure and Response Prevention)**—not just therapists who list “anxiety/OCD” among many specialties. The following look like strong Texas telehealth options based on their publicly listed OCD focus, ERP training, and self-pay information. This isn’t a personal endorsement, and availability/rates can change.

### Strong private-pay options

| Therapist/practice | Why consider them | Listed private-pay rate |
|---|---|---:|
| **Loni Itah, MA, LPC — Resilience Room Counseling** | OCD is a primary focus; uses ERP, ACT, CBT, and I-CBT; telehealth throughout Texas; IOCDF BTTI-trained; works with teens 15+ and adults. | **$225 per 50-minute session** ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/itah-loni/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Lukas Snear, LPC — Azimuth OCD and Anxiety** | OCD is his exclusive focus; IOCDF BTTI-trained; treats many OCD presentations via telehealth across Texas. | **$250/session**; sliding scale and limited scholarships may be available. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/snear-lukas/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Lindy Noll, LCSW — Focus Integrated Psychotherapy** | Virtual therapy for adults statewide; IOCDF BTTI-trained and ERP-focused. | **$175 per 50-minute session**. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/providers/noll-lindy/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Dr. Erikalin Ashton — Austin Center for Anxiety** | Online CBT/ERP for OCD and panic for adults in Texas; psychologist; clear self-pay pricing. | **$150 per 45-minute session**, $175 initial evaluation. ([austinanxietycenter.com](https://www.austinanxietycenter.com/insurance-fees?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Tina Smith, LPC — Ray of Hope Counseling** | 100% online ERP therapy anywhere in Texas; clear self-pay rate. | **$150 per 45–50-minute session**. ([rohcounselingtx.com](https://www.rohcounselingtx.com/services/erp-therapy?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Jen Herz, LCSW — Herz Psychotherapy** | ERP for adolescents and adults; telehealth across Texas; private-pay practice with sliding-scale availability. | **Starting at $185/session**. ([herzpsychotherapy.com](https://herzpsychotherapy.com/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Steven Sainato, LPC — Sainato Counseling** | Telehealth throughout Texas and uses ERP/ACT; potentially more budget-friendly. | **$135/session**. ([sainatocounseling.com](https://sainatocounseling.com/about?utm_source=openai)) |

### My practical shortlist

- **Most OCD-specialized:** Lukas Snear or Loni Itah  
- **Good balance of specialization and price:** Lindy Noll, Erikalin Ashton, or Tina Smith  
- **Lower-cost option:** Steven Sainato; also ask Azimuth about its supervised reduced-fee program, which lists **$40–$150/session** depending on household income. ([azimuthocd.com](https://www.azimuthocd.com/reduced-fee-counseling?utm_source=openai))  
- **If you want a psychologist rather than an LPC/LCSW:** Erikalin Ashton or another psychologist from the IOCDF directory may be worth considering.

### Questions to ask before booking

1. **How much of your practice is OCD treatment?**
2. **Do you use ERP every week, including exposures between sessions?**
3. **How do you treat mental compulsions, reassurance-seeking, rumination, or “Pure O”?**
4. **Do you work with my particular presentation—scrupulosity, relationship OCD, sexual intrusive thoughts, health OCD, harm OCD, contamination, real-event OCD, or sensorimotor OCD?**
5. **What is the full self-pay cost, including intake, missed appointments, and between-session support?**
6. **Will you provide a Good Faith Estimate and/or superbill?** You can explicitly say that you do **not** want them to bill your insurance.

For telehealth, you generally need to be physically located in Texas during the session, so confirm that the clinician is currently licensed and able to see clients in your part of the state.
